story: On a breezy, clear Tuesday morning at 7:17, Gary sits at his workbench filling out the Architectural Review form for his parade lights and speaker mounts, looking determined. Across the way, Donna is excited as she texts Gary to confirm pickleball and books a two-hour court slot on her phone. Over at his porch, Hal keeps his binoculars trained on Donna's flamingos, determined to get an accurate count. Meanwhile, Rosa, content but focused, checks her shift schedule and makes sure Thursday at 8 AM stays free for coffee with Hal.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Fill out the Architectural Review form, listing the parade lights and speaker mounts
Donna (donna phone): Text Gary to confirm Tuesday pickleball and book a two-hour court slot
Hal (hal binoculars): Count Donna's flamingos from the porch
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Check this week's per-diem shifts and make sure Thursday 8 AM stays clear for coffee with Hal

gary.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM on Tuesday and I'm home with the Architectural Review form in hand. Memory says I headed to Town Square last tick, but my surroundings say I'm back in my own house, so I'll work with what's in front of me. Donna and I planned Tuesday morning pickleball and coffee at Rosa's, and I don't want to be late. Before that, the smart move is to fill out this form while it's fresh, listing the lights and sound system honestly. L-01 says visible cart mods need approval, and Donna and Hal were right to steer me that way. L-03 is also on my mind: no amplified sound before 7 AM, and it's just past that now, but I'll still test the sound system quietly. The golf cart is right here, so I'll sit at the workbench with the cart, measure my planned light strips and speaker mounts, and get the form filled out properly.

parameters.content: Fill out the Architectural Review form, listing the parade lights and speaker mounts

donna.thought_process: It's Tuesday morning, 7:17, and today is the big pickleball session with Gary. I'm home alone, so there's no one to talk to right now. My bag, calendar, and phone are right here. Since Gary has never actually played, the smartest thing is to text him a friendly confirmation and get him to the courts on time. L-05 caps court reservations at 2 hours, so I should book a slot within that limit. A quick text keeps things moving without nagging anyone in person.

parameters.content: Text Gary to confirm Tuesday pickleball and book a two-hour court slot

hal.thought_process: Another morning, and I'm home with nobody in sight. My goal is to cross-check the flamingo tally against L-02 and have my paperwork in order for the committee. The binoculars are right here, so I'll start the day's inspection of Donna's lawn before any lines get said. I'll log the count in my violation notebook afterward and then head to Town Hall with a clean report.

parameters.content: Count Donna's flamingos from the porch

rosa.thought_process: It's Tuesday morning, 7:17 AM, and the dinner went well. I promised Hal coffee Thursday at eight on my porch, written in ink. Before I do anything else, I should check the shift schedule so I don't double-book myself like I keep doing. Nobody's around, so the schedule is the obvious thing to touch.

parameters.content: Check this week's per-diem shifts and make sure Thursday 8 AM stays clear for coffee with Hal

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
